newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tietmeyer-Revaluing gold would not yield payout.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer-Revaluing gold would not yield payout.

text.p: Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer said on Sunday that revaluing gold lodged at the Bundesbank would not under current rules yield any payout to the government.

In an interview with German radio, Tietmeyer also stressed that while the sale of gold reserves would in theory generate a payout, this was not an option for the German central bank and there was no pressure from Bonn to do so.

Asked how Finance Minister Theo Waigel could benefit from Bundesbank gold reserves, Tietmeyer said: "According to the rules applying, this would only work if gold reserves were to be sold. But the government has made clear that it will not in any way force the Bundesbank to sell gold. To that extent it is not an issue at all."

The Bundesbank has reached an agreement with the government over revaluing currency reserves lodged at the central bank which will not generate any extraordinary payout to Bonn this year, the crucial year for the choice of participants in monetary union.
The central bank earlier shot down a plan by Waigel to use revaluation of reserves to ease Germany's path to monetary union.
Tietmeyer repeated that the compromise reached with Bonn, viewed widely as a come-down for the government, was a "good and acceptable solution."
